title: Understanding Bluff and Fold in Texas Hold'em
summaryJa: ポーカーの「ブラフ」は弱いハンドで強いふりをする戦略であり、相手が「フォールド」することを狙ったテクニックです。この二つは対立する重要な概念で、成功したブラフにより勝利することができます。
segments: In Texas Hold'em poker, a bluff is when you bet or raise with a weak hand. You try to make other players think you have a strong hand.
A bluff is a strategy. Sometimes players bluff to win the pot without showing their cards.
Here is a simple example. You have two cards that are not very good.
The flop comes. You do not have a strong hand.
But you bet like you have a strong hand. You want other players to think you are strong.
If they believe you, they will fold their cards. Fold means to quit the hand.
When you fold, you give up your cards. You lose the money you already put in the pot.
But you do not lose more money. For example, another player bets.
You think their hand is stronger. You do not want to lose more money.
So you fold. Bluff and fold are connected.
When you bluff, you hope other players will fold. When players fold, they do not see your cards.
This is the goal of a good bluff. A successful bluff helps you win the pot.
A bad bluff can cost you money. So good players only bluff at the right time.
